title: Cold rebuild: Sell two seats, safely
summary: Rebuild Sell two seats, safely from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You wrote **Sell two seats, safely** in *Lost updates and isolation levels*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Event 3 has 1 seat left. What does the last line return?
code: UPDATE events SET seats_left = seats_left - 2 WHERE id = 3 AND seats_left >= 2;
SELECT seats_left, changes() FROM events WHERE id = 3;
setup: CREATE TABLE events (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, venue TEXT NOT NULL, starts_at TEXT NOT NULL, capacity INTEGER NOT NULL, seats_left INTEGER NOT NULL, price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, event_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES events(id), customer TEXT NOT NULL, qty INTEGER NOT NULL, placed_at TEXT NOT NULL);
steps.explain: Not enough seats, so the guard in WHERE matches nothing: 0 rows changed, and the 1 seat stays.

prompt: A customer orders **2** tickets for event **3**. Write the single `UPDATE` that takes 2 seats **only if at least 2 are left**, and otherwise changes nothing.
Tables: `events(id, name, venue, starts_at, capacity, seats_left, price_cents)`, `orders(id, event_id, customer, qty, placed_at)`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
